messages:
maya: @support urgent — ACME's indexer failed during the scheduled backfill at ~10:12 PST. error from vector DB: "vector size mismatch: expected 768, got 512". they paused the job. customer is upset about failed writes and billing for retries.

support-aly: can you paste the exact error and the model param used for embeddings? also need the job id and any recent config changes.

maya: job id: backfill-acme-2026-03-14-2. logs:
```
IndexerClient.WriteError: rejected 233/1200 vectors
caused_by: VectorDimensionError(expected=768, found=512)
trace: indexer/worker.go:142 indexer/insert.go:87
```
They ran the backfill against /v1/embeddings with model=opena-embed-lite-512 (customer used an older model alias from their script). But our default in the backfill runner should be opena-embed-768. We recently ran a lightweight model rollout for cost-saving; not sure if job picked it up.

liam: interesting — runtime note: a rolling config change happened at 09:59 where we introduced a new model alias mapping that can route requests to cheaper 512-dim variant for small accounts. That mapping should only apply to hosted inference, not to explicit model parameter in tasks. Did the backfill rely on alias resolution?

maya: their backfill code was using generic alias "embedding-default" (not pinned). So yes, it likely picked the new alias mapping.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-345 (priority=P2) — Autocreated by alert: indexer-dim-mismatch-ingest. Please add owners.

sre-jen: observed a latency spike and increased retries coincident with the alias rollout at 09:59. Batching patterns shifted — some workers started sending mixed-dim batches when retry logic retried with a different model variant. That mixed batch appears to cause the vector DB error path.

db-indexer: quick context from the index side: our index schema is strict: vector_dim = 768. We intentionally reject mismatched vectors because downstream ANN assumptions break. We can add a shim to automatically reject earlier with clearer logs or to perform a compatibility transform (pad/truncate). But quality risk if dimensions padded.

support-aly: customer message: "We started a backfill and saw many failures. Our bill spiked because of retries. Please pause and advise next steps." They want a timeline and refund for failed quota.

liam: mitigation options: 1) immediately pause backfill job (maya can coordinate). 2) revert alias mapping so new requests don't get 512 variant. 3) run a small canary backfill with pinned 768 model and verify. 4) provide ACME a one-time credit for failed attempts.

maya: pausing job now. (actioned)

maya: repro steps to reproduce locally for engineering:
1) clone backfill runner and set MODEL_ALIAS=embedding-default
2) run small job against staging indexer with alias mapping active
3) observe indexer rejects with VectorDimensionError

curl example to reproduce (use staging key):
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.staging/v1/embeddings \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $STAGING_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"embedding-default","input":["hello world"]}'
```
expected: 768-dim vector. actual: 512-dim vector when alias resolves to opena-embed-lite-512.

python quick repro (embedding client):
```python
from redwood import EmbeddingsClient
client = EmbeddingsClient(api_key="$STAGING_KEY")
resp = client.create(model="embedding-default", input=["hello world"])
print(len(resp.data[0].embedding))  # 512 vs 768
```

liam: immediate action: I'm rolling back the alias mapping now to ensure alias->768. will confirm when done. then we'll run a canary.

ops-bot: deploy: alias-mapping-revert by liam at 2026-03-14T10:26:45Z — success :white_check_mark: 

liam: revert complete. please re-run canary. If canary is green, we need to decide whether to: a) pin backfill to 768 model, b) add dim check in runner to fail early with clearer messaging, c) add a compatibility adapter to pad 512->768 for legacy clients (not ideal).

db-indexer: prefer b + c as short-term: dim check + opt-in pad transform for customers that explicitly accept quality tradeoff. we'll schedule schema-tolerant ingest later.

support-aly: I'll tell ACME we paused the job, rolled back the alias, and will run a canary. Offering a credit for failed writes and retries. Can someone estimate credit amount? finance-ravi please advise.

finance-ravi: need charge logs for backfill-acme-2026-03-14-2 and counts of failed vs successful tokens. I'll start a billing audit and propose a provisional credit.

maya: canary run started against staging indexer with model pinned to opena-embed-768. will report results.

sre-jen: note for postmortem: root cause looks like configuration leak (alias applied to backfill runner due to env inheritance) + lack of pre-ingest dim validation in runner. We'll add a checklist.

maya: canary result: OK — vectors now 768 and index accepts writes. No errors after 2000 vectors.

liam: next steps (short):
- liam: add explicit dim check to backfill runner (fail fast and surface clear error) — ETA EOD today
- db-indexer: add an opt-in padding transform and better logging — ETA 48h
- support-aly: comms and credit offer to ACME — send by EOD
- finance-ravi: preliminary credit estimate in 4h
- maya: coordinate resume only after we confirm pinned-model backfill

maya: assigning owners in thread: liam (runtime changes), db-indexer (ingest shim), support-aly (customer comms), finance-ravi (billing). :spiral_calendar_pad:

ops-bot: note: auto-ticket created in Jira: REDW-INDX-789 for indexer padding shim.

cust-rep-ethan: ACME acknowledges the update and appreciates the quick rollback. Requested an ETA for full backfill completion and confirmation that model will be pinned.

liam: ETA for canary -> full backfill: if no further issues, we can run full backfill tomorrow morning window. Will make runner explicitly pin model param in backfill config.

maya: closing loop here — will reopen thread if any regression during full run. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
